newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower on late selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower on late selling.

text.p: Late profit-taking pulled Taiwan share prices to a slightly lower close on Friday in active trade but brokers said they did not expect major near-term losses.

Buying was inspired in early trade by Chinese President Jiang Zemin's Thursday comments that political differences would not affect Taiwan-China trade and investment. But selling started at mid-session as players saw no sign of foreign funds entry before September 2, when Morgan Stanley is set to include Taiwan into its global stock indices, brokers said.
The weighted index declined 2.61 points or 0.04 percent to close at 6,309.82. Turnover was T$50.46 billion.

"Many people have high expectations for foreign funds because of the Morgan Stanley indices," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming. "When they saw no signs of foreign fund movements, selling was the best option for them."
If foreign institutions decrease holdings in coming days, individual investors may follow suit, brokers said.
"But major falls are not likely because there is some good news about Taiwan-China investment and that should support the market," said Huang Shou-shan of Foremost Investment Services.
China-concept shares could remain focus of the market, brokers said.
Evergreen Marine jumped the daily seven percent limit to T$54 on hopes for imminent direct shipping links with China.
Yulon Motor, which reported a 54 percent year-on-year jump in first half pre-tax profits, rose 80 cents to T$22.7.
Brokers said the overnight declines on the Wall Street, which dampened sentiment on many Asian markets on Friday, had little impact in Taiwan, which is preoccupied with China.
A 6,250-6,350 trading range was seen in coming sessions.
